question_text: Every instruction passes through four stages: fetch, decode, execute and write-back. Each stage takes exactly one clock cycle and there are no stalls. Calculate the number of clock cycles needed: (i) to complete 10 instructions on one core with no pipelining, where an instruction starts only after the previous one has finished; (ii) to complete 10 instructions on one core with a four-stage pipeline; (iii) to complete 40 independent instructions shared equally between four pipelined cores that run in parallel.
adaptation_rationale: Original question written by Claude (single-agent Chunk 3 continuation, 2026-11-04) for a syllabus statement with no linked question at handover; no historical source question or official marking status claimed.
solution: (i) 10 x 4 = 40 cycles. (ii) 4 cycles for the first instruction, then 1 more for each of the remaining 9: 4 + 9 = 13 cycles. (iii) each core completes 10 instructions in 13 cycles and the cores run at the same time, so 13 cycles.

marking_points.criterion: (iii) 13 cycles, recognising that the four cores each complete 10 instructions simultaneously.

acceptable_alternatives: Follow-through in (iii) from an incorrect (ii) if the parallel reasoning (same time as one core with 10 instructions) is correct.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 3 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.

verification.scope: Idealised model: no hazards, stalls, memory delays or scheduling overhead. Complements O-C3-A-001 descriptive coverage.
